content: The Institute of Medicine (IOM) is a non-profit, non-governmental organization in the United States that operates as part of the National Academies. It was established in 1970 under the charter of the National Academy of Sciences. The primary mission of the IOM is to provide expert, independent advice on matters related to biomedical science, medicine, and health. The IOM relies on a volunteer workforce composed of scientists and employs a rigorous peer review process. Each report produced by the IOM undergoes evaluation by external experts, whose identities remain confidential until the publication of the study. While the majority of the IOM’s studies are commissioned and funded by the U.S. federal government, other organizations can also request studies, and the IOM itself initiates some projects. The current President of the IOM is Dr. Harvey V. Fineberg, M.D., Ph.D. The organization addresses a wide range of topics, including mental health, child health, food and nutrition, aging, women’s health, education, public policy, healthcare quality, diseases, global health, workplace health, military and veterans’ health, health sciences, environmental health, treatment, public health and prevention, and minority health. The IOM serves as both a research institution and an honorary membership organization. Its members are elected based on their professional accomplishments and their ability to contribute to the organization’s mission. These members, along with other experts, participate in IOM studies, workshops, and other activities without receiving financial compensation. The IOM’s reports are made freely accessible to the public through the National Academies Press, which is the publishing division of the United States National Academies. These reports are available in various formats online.
